question: Do naturally formed four-particle rings preserve material isolation better than the SAME world after a controlled single-bond opening?
null_hypothesis: No consistent advantage for the untouched ring versus opened variants under tested initial states.
physical_laws: original M6, no modifications to simulator, chemistry, movement, energy decay or RNG

sampling.source: M6.4 zero-initial-bond natural world with 24x24 periodic grid and existing baseline/enriched species counts
sampling.selection: First two distinct material-ID sets forming a four-cycle in each world, ordered by first observed tick then sorted IDs. Do not replace missing cases.
sampling.clone: Exact independently cloned complete snapshot with same source particle IDs, bonds, energy, RNG state and draws, and all source reservoirs and accounting.
sampling.opening: Remove lowest-sorted source-ID bond or its disjoint opposite and credit its *stored bond energy* to the two endpoint particles (floor-half, remainder). The already dissipated formation energy stays dissipated. World.check() must pass; this is an initial-condition perturbation, NOT a change in the evolution laws.
sampling.exact_signature: src/alife/structures.py signature_v2 for simple cycles, old historical signature() unchanged

outcomes.primary: At followup step 120, all original ring particle IDs must remain a single connected aggregate with exactly the same four IDs and no outsiders. Ring topology at the endpoint is NOT required.
secondary: Total ticks with exactly the original isolated four-particle connected aggregate, regardless of current ring or chain form
First loss of isolated four-material component (due to attachment or fragmentation) and later restoration, with right censoring
Time until reappearance of the exact four-ID cycle after opening
Hashes, RNG fingerprint and draws, total energy/dissipation, bond formation and break counts of each arm
Natural precursor ring signature, original occurrence tick and materials; all missing cases preserved
outcomes.exposed_confounders: Opening changes topology, available valence and energy allocation. Its later RNG trajectory may diverge. Therefore an effect reflects the full specified physical perturbation, NOT topology alone.
outcomes.pairing: Compare three arms from each exact selected world snapshot. Selected rings from one world may be correlated. Never call them independent universes for statistical inference.

decision.pass: Both densities must show keep_ring isolated-at-120 rate minus open_lowest_edge rate >=0.20; open_opposite_edge must have positive rate difference in both densities. If enough pairs, call only 'ring_closure_protection_signal', not heredity.
decision.fail: Otherwise 'no_robust_ring_closure_protection' or 'underpowered'; do not change seeds or threshold post hoc.
